haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes. If unclaimed, the reservation expires and stock returns to sale; the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT until a payment outcome.
haiku-low.q2: Reserved before charging. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing, the order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK with the short items, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: Payment sends the charge with the order id as idempotency key, so retries use the same key and cannot double-charge.
haiku-low.q4: Order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and RefundRequested is published; Payment automatically refunds the full amount, and the customer is emailed.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is not emptied; ordered lines are removed after OrderConfirmed. Items added later stay. On checkout failure the cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q6: Order moves checkout through steps via conditional updates and calls; the order's status row in Order records how far it got.
haiku-low.q7: Provider webhooks Payment; Payment records the outcome and writes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined to its outbox, which the relay publishes for Order.
haiku-low.q8: Payment records provider event ids in a dedupe table; Order uses conditional status updates. Duplicates change nothing and publish nothing.
haiku-low.q9: Order's PaymentDeclined handler conditionally sets PAYMENT_FAILED and, if that changed the order, tells Inventory to release the hold.
haiku-low.q10: Lapsed stock is re-taken if still free, so the order is fulfilled; only if the claim fails is it cancelled and refunded.
haiku-low.q11: Payment's refund record (REFUND_PENDING, attempt count, next retry time) is retried with backoff; at the limit it becomes REFUND_FAILED, alerts on-call, and retries slowly.
haiku-low.q12: Order publishes OrderConfirmed when the order becomes CONFIRMED; Cart removes only the ordered lines and quantities.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes from creation (reservation row ACTIVE, expires in 10 min). If not claimed in time, the Inventory sweeper (every minute) marks it EXPIRED and stock goes back on sale; it triggers nothing else, and the order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before any payment. If any line is short, Inventory reserves nothing (all-or-nothing in one local transaction) and returns the short items; order becomes REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, no payment is requested, cart unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The charge request uses an idempotency key equal to the order id, and retries reuse the same key, so the provider does not charge twice.
sonnet.q4: Inventory replies 'claim failed'. Order moves PAID to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK (conditional) and writes RefundRequested (OUT_OF_STOCK) plus a customer email to the outbox. Payment automatically refunds the full amount to the original payment method; the order's refund field later becomes REFUNDED.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when the order is CONFIRMED: Cart removes exactly the ordered lines and quantities on the OrderConfirmed event (later-added items stay). On any failure (short stock, decline, unavailable, cancel) the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order service drives the flow (calls Inventory, reacts to Payment events, runs its sweeper). The record of progress is the order status stored in Order's orders table (plus the refund field); payment and reservation states are also kept in Payment and Inventory.
sonnet.q7: Provider sends a webhook to Payment (or Payment's 35-minute poller asks the provider). Payment updates the payment and writes PaymentSucceeded/PaymentDeclined to its outbox; the relay publishes it on the broker, and Order consumes it.
sonnet.q8: Several layers: Payment records provider event ids in a unique-constrained dedupe table (duplicate gets 200 and nothing done); state changes are conditional updates that change nothing on a repeat so nothing is published; Order ignores events for statuses showing a repeat; claim and refund calls are keyed by order id; Cart records handled order ids; one refund record per order id.
sonnet.q9: Order handles PaymentDeclined by setting PAYMENT_FAILED (only if still AWAITING_PAYMENT); if that changed the order, it calls Inventory to release the hold (retried until ok). Release turns ACTIVE to RELEASED; otherwise a no-op. If it never works, the 10-minute expiry frees the stock.
sonnet.q10: At claim, Inventory checks the reservation. If it is EXPIRED or RELEASED but all lines can be taken again now, the same row becomes CLAIMED and the order is fulfilled; if the stock has gone, the claim fails and the order is cancelled and refunded.
sonnet.q11: The refund record stays REFUND_PENDING in Payment's refunds table (with attempt count and next-retry time); the retrier retries every minute with backoff using the same idempotency key. At the retry limit it becomes REFUND_FAILED, alerts on-call, goes to a manual queue, and is still retried at a slow fixed interval until a human closes it.
sonnet.q12: Order's OrderConfirmed event (carrying cart id and lines), published when the order becomes CONFIRMED; the Cart service removes those lines and records the order id in its handled-order table.
